issues.description: Pipeline node iteration example uses next() over a generator without justification, obscuring intent
issues.detail: The snippet `training_node = next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` is needlessly clever for documentation. A reader learning the API should see `training_node = pipeline.nodes[0]` or an explicit name lookup. The generator expression suggests filtering that isn't happening. Literate code teaches the reader; this teaches a bad habit.

issues.description: ImagePreview example contains unreachable code after return statement
issues.detail: Lines showing `return ImagePreview(content="https://...")` followed by a commented alternative `return` are technically fine as comments, but the structure reads as if both branches execute. A careful reader pauses. Split into two distinct example functions, or use an `if/else` on a parameter. Clarity for the reader is the constraint.

issues.description: CustomPreview example uses `[...]` ellipsis literals that are not valid placeholders for the reader
issues.detail: `"nodes": [...], "edges": [...]` is Python-legal (Ellipsis in a list) but semantically misleading in a tutorial — readers may copy it and wonder why their renderer fails. Use `[]` with a comment `# list of node dicts`, or show one concrete element. Documentation code should be copy-paste-correct or visibly incomplete.

issues.description: Closure example for data context omits the `name=` argument used elsewhere, breaking consistency
issues.detail: Earlier pipeline examples include `name="train_model_node"` on every `node(...)` call; the closure example at the end drops it. Either the name is required or it isn't — a reader cannot tell from the docs. Pick one convention and apply it uniformly. Consistency is part of readability.

issues.description: Mermaid `meta` config mixes Mermaid-native keys with a Kedro-Viz-specific `textStyle` key without flagging the distinction
issues.detail: `securityLevel`, `flowchart`, `themeVariables` are Mermaid config keys; `textStyle` appears to be a Kedro-Viz extension. Linking to the Mermaid schema then including a non-schema key will confuse the careful reader who checks the link. Annotate which keys are passthrough-to-Mermaid versus Kedro-Viz-only.

issues.description: Several standalone `node(...)` examples are not wrapped in `Pipeline([...])` and lack imports, so they will not run as shown
issues.detail: The Mermaid-config and code-preview examples present bare `node(func=..., preview_fn=...)` calls outside any pipeline and without re-importing `node`. A reader copying these will get `NameError` or an orphan node. Either show them inside a `Pipeline([...])` block (matching the Basic Usage section) or mark the snippet as a fragment.

review.summary: The documentation is well-organized and covers the preview API surface thoroughly, with appropriate experimental-feature warning. However, as literate teaching material it has rough edges that a careful reader will trip over: an unnecessarily clever `next()` over a generator, unreachable-looking return statements in one example, `[...]` placeholders that are legal Python but misleading, inconsistent use of the `name=` argument across examples, and bare `node(...)` snippets divorced from any `Pipeline([...])` context. None of these are wrong; all of them reduce the reader's confidence that they understand the API. The Mermaid config section also conflates passthrough Mermaid keys with Kedro-Viz extensions without saying so. Fixes are small and mechanical — verdict: UNDER-AUDITED for reader-facing clarity, but RIGOROUS in scope coverage.
